neutralAnnualChoices: Retain the existing official-order annual illustration: Russia and Caribbean lectures, Africa health/climate and Philip II research seminars, papyrological sources and digital cartography. All remain members of the respective current required-choice menus. One 5-EC lecture, 10-EC seminar and 5-EC source/method option per semester; no route selected to fit UCR. Annual examples do not guarantee future titles.
currentPrimaryFindings: First-year surveys and historical labs provide chronological/regional, primary-source and source-critical study. Two required 10-EC research seminars teach question formulation, literature/source analysis, written papers and presentations, with increasing independence.

European History covers Renaissance–1815 and 19th century onward; World History connects Africa, Americas, China and South Asia through empire, hierarchy, authority, trade and migration. Economic/Social History is a genuine long-run European/Dutch survey with historical labs, not economic theory by title.

Citizens and Subjects traces membership, exclusion and citizenship from antiquity to the present. Global Connections studies global-history methods and multi-scale trade, migration, institutions, imperialism and cultural/technological connections.

Papyrological Sources explicitly uses translated texts and requires no Greek, Latin or Egyptian language; its specialist textual corpus/method still has no dedicated selected UCR counterpart. Digital Cartography teaches QGIS and historical primary-source datasets/maps.

Africa seminar concerns medical/epidemiological and environmental/colonial history; African Art is not a substitute merely because both concern Africa. Philip II studies the Spanish king, power, personality, religion, dynasty and historiography; not a Dutch-history survey.
The current root still labels its old route seminar/lecture/15-EC thesis as outgoing. No revised final-work weight or route-dependent entry rule is imported.
